title: Social class in the UK and the US

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps translating the words below.

atoms.b: The elite class in the UK is ((heritage-based heritage_based based_on_heritage)) and characterized by deep historical roots. Class identity is primarily shaped by ((family_background)), accent, regional dialects and education, rather than just financial wealth and occupation.

Elite private schools often provide the ((social_network)) necessary for high-ranking jobs. Therefore, social mobility can be limited by cultural barriers that are difficult to overcome, and a distinct ((working-class working_class)) identity remains strong in many regions.

atoms.b: The class system in the US is primarily defined by income, ((occupation job)), education, and lifestyle, with far less focus on family lineage. In theory, the “American Dream” promises ((social_mobility)) based on individual work. In reality, the US is one of the least socially mobile countries because a good education is very expensive.
((Accents accents)) indicate region more than social class. Furthermore, ((social_identity)) in the US is strongly shaped by a history of migration and racial diversity.

atoms.a: Dialects are deeply tied to regional identity and accents indicate social class.
Historically, aristocracy played a significant role, with titles indicating upper class.
Because accents have historically signalled social class, they are more stigmatized.
High social mobility for everybody in theory, but not always in practice.
Schooling and education is seen as very important for future success.
Social class is less openly discussed but still influential.
Class identity is more explicit and culturally recognised.
Social class is less focused on family lineage, but more on what you earn and achieve.
